# discord_channel_member_permissions (Data Source)

Reads a member's permissions in a channel as Discord computes them from all of the member's roles and `@everyone`, applying the channel's overwrites for them and for the member. Threads use their parent channel's overwrites. The bot needs `VIEW_CHANNEL` in the channel, and `CONNECT` as well in voice and stage channels. See [Get Channel Member Permissions](https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/channel#get-channel-member-permissions).

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "discord_current_user" "bot" {}

# The bot's permissions in a channel, after the channel's overwrites.
data "discord_channel_member_permissions" "bot_announcements" {
  channel_id = var.announcements_channel_id
  user_id    = data.discord_current_user.bot.id
}

check "bot_can_post_announcements" {
  assert {
    condition     = contains(data.discord_channel_member_permissions.bot_announcements.permission_names, "SEND_MESSAGES")
    error_message = "The bot cannot send messages in the announcements channel."
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `channel_id` (String) ID of the channel or thread.
- `user_id` (String) ID of the member's user.

### Optional

- `implicit` (Boolean) Whether Discord masks the permissions that a missing `VIEW_CHANNEL`, or a missing `CONNECT` in a voice or stage channel, makes unusable (see [implicit permissions](https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/permissions#implicit-permissions)). Defaults to `true`. Discord never masks the permissions of bot members.

### Read-Only

- `permission_names` (Set of String) Names of the permission flags set in `permissions`, such as `VIEW_CHANNEL`. Flags this provider does not know are omitted.
- `permissions` (String) The computed permissions as a decimal bitfield string.
